Class multihop needs a memory the prompt cannot reach without the first. natural and disjoint were written by a second model that saw each note alone (openai/gpt-6.1-sol); the rest were authored with the memories, so those are a guide rather than a benchmark.

memories.body: Never run destructive migrations against the shared staging database without asking in #infra first.
Invoice amounts are integer cents, never floats, because a rounding bug double-charged customers.
The billing webhook retries for 72 hours, so handlers must be idempotent.
The deploy pipeline reads the version from packages/core/package.json, not the root package.json.
This workspace is bun-only; npm rewrites the lockfile.
Integration tests must hit a real SQLite database. A mocked migration once passed while production failed.
Keep commits small with one logical change each.
The maintainer reviews on a phone, so keep pull request descriptions under ten lines.
CI runs only on Node 22.
Bedrock provider tests need AWS_PROFILE=eval or they hang indefinitely.
The on-call latency board is https://grafana.internal/d/ingest.
The session store stays in SQLite rather than Postgres because the extension must work offline.
The public API stays on v2 until the mobile app ships its next release.
Do not add comments that restate the code.
Background jobs must never use the session model, only an explicitly configured model.
All timestamps in the ledger are stored in UTC; conversions happen only in the web client.
test/sync.test.ts is flaky on macOS because of fsevents latency; rerun it before debugging.
Never log customer email addresses; the compliance audit failed on this in 2025.
HTTP clients use exponential backoff with full jitter, capped at 30 seconds.
Feature flags live in config/flags.yaml and must have an owner and a removal date.
User-facing strings go through t() from packages/i18n; hard-coded English fails review.
Static assets are served from Cloudflare R2; the purge script is tools/purge.mjs.
Secrets come from 1Password via op run; .env files are forbidden in the repo.
The Stripe sandbox allows 25 requests per second; load tests must stay under that.
List endpoints use cursor pagination; offset pagination broke on large tenants.
API errors use {error:{code,message}}; never return a bare string.
Shared types live in packages/contracts; services must not import each other directly.
Scheduled jobs run through Temporal, not cron, so that retries are visible.
Transactional email goes through Postmark; marketing email must never use that account.
Long-running migrations take an advisory lock; check pg_locks before assuming a hang.
The notifier service deploys through the Tern pipeline.
Tern needs its VPN token rotated before any production run; tokens last 12 hours.
The reconciliation job is owned by the Harbor team.
Harbor only accepts change requests through the CAB form on Thursdays.
Refunds call the ledger-core service synchronously.
ledger-core has a 500 ms budget; anything slower trips its circuit breaker.
The export feature stores files in the Osprey bucket.
Osprey objects expire after 7 days under the retention policy.
Invoice PDFs are rendered by the Quill worker.
Quill crashes on fonts above 24 MB and has to be restarted by hand with tools/quill-reset.mjs.
Customer search is backed by the Beryl index.
Beryl reindexing needs a maintenance window announced 48 hours ahead.
Mobile push notifications go through the Kestrel gateway.
Kestrel silently drops payloads above 3 KB.
Tax calculation uses the Sable library.
Sable is pinned at 4.2 because 4.3 changed rounding for Swiss VAT.
Single sign-on is handled by the Juniper proxy.
Juniper sessions are sticky, so blue-green cutovers log users out unless drained first.
The fraud score comes from the Wren model endpoint.
Wren costs 4 cents a call, so never call it in a loop.
